title: Quantitative of progesterone using isotope dilution-matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization-time of flight mass spectrometry
author: Yang, You, et al.
materials: (1)Human serum was collected in sterile tubes and centrifuged at 1000 g for 10 min at 4 °C.(2)1 mL of the supernatant was adjusted to pH 9.8 ± 0.2 with 0.1 g/mL carbonate/bicarbonate buffer [1].(3)An incorporation of 13C3-Progesterone (15 ng/mL, Sigma-Aldrich, USA) was added as the internal standard isotope.

(1)5 µL of each serum progesterone sample described above was mixed with 1 µL of the matrix, 2,5-Dihydroxybenzoic acid (DHB, Sigma-Aldrich, USA) [4].(2)Deposited on the sample tray at room temperature. After the sample-matrix mix was dried, the tray was subjected to measurement and generally 100 laser shots were used in the analytical process. All the samples were measured in triplicate.

steps.title: Prepare serum and add internal standard
steps.instruction: Collect human serum in sterile tubes, centrifuge at 1000 g for 10 min at 4 °C; transfer 1 mL supernatant and adjust pH to 9.8 ± 0.2 with 0.1 g/mL carbonate/bicarbonate buffer; add 13C3‑Progesterone internal standard to a final concentration of 15 ng/mL (Sigma‑Aldrich, USA).

steps.title: Extract progesterone by SPE
steps.instruction: Pre‑equilibrate a SPE Supra‑Clean 300 Å C4 column (PerkinElmer, USA) with methanol followed by double‑distilled water; load the prepared serum sample onto the column and discard the flow‑through; wash the column with 2 mL double‑distilled water; elute progesterone with 4 mL methanol; evaporate the eluate to dryness using centrifugal evaporation.

steps.title: Prepare MALDI sample and acquire spectrum
steps.instruction: Mix 5 µL of the dried progesterone extract with 1 µL of 2,5‑Dihydroxybenzoic acid (DHB) matrix (Sigma‑Aldrich, USA); deposit the mixture onto a MALDI sample tray at room temperature and allow it to dry; acquire MALDI‑TOF MS data using approximately 100 laser shots per spot; measure each sample in triplicate.
